about.headline: Automation that feels like child's play
about.heroBody: We believe industrial automation shouldn’t be complicated. Bioversee makes it easy to get started, whether you’re a DIY maker, a student, or a professional in the field.
about.productTitle: The same lab in your pocket
about.productBody: Devices, inbox, and account, with live updates so you can respond from anywhere.
about.webTitle: Control your process from the browser
about.webBody: Pump switches and motion knobs on the left, live sensor charts on the right, and your bioreactor in the middle. Built for monitoring and control in one view.
about.phoneCaption: Tap Devices, Inbox, or Account to explore the app, the same way you would on your phone.
about.piBody: Download the Bioversee app for Raspberry Pi, sign in on the device, connect your bioreactor, and control it from the website.
about.piCaption: A compact edge device for local monitoring and control when you are next to the process.
about.piGateSorry: Sorry, but this part of Bioversee is still under construction.
about.storyLede: Bioversee is built on a simple premise backed by decades of research: engineers learn, operate, and keep processes safe when they can see how a plant behaves, not only when they read about it.
about.evidenceTeachBody: Cognitive research shows people understand complex systems more deeply from words combined with pictures than from words alone (Mayer’s multimedia principle). In chemical and biochemical engineering, pedagogical process simulators and virtual laboratories are now recognized as core tools for linking models to industrial practice, especially where real plants are costly, slow, or unsafe for experimentation.
about.evidenceSafetyBody: Process safety depends on how operators see the plant. Ecological Interface Design shows that displays which make process constraints and relationships visible help operators detect faults and respond to unanticipated events. Those findings were later confirmed with professional operators on industrial petrochemical simulators. Industry standards such as ANSI/ISA-101.01 treat well-designed HMIs as a lever for safer, more effective control under normal and abnormal conditions.
about.evidenceProcessBody: Process systems engineering educators argue that digitalization makes model-based thinking and interactive simulation more important than ever in the curriculum. Bioversee follows that line: an affordable, playful process visualization for industry training and a serious educational instrument for engineering students.
about.ref1: Mayer, R. E. Multimedia Learning. Cambridge University Press. Multimedia principle: deeper learning from words and pictures than from words alone.
about.ref2: Vicente, K. J. & Rasmussen, J. (1992). Ecological interface design: Theoretical foundations. IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics, 22(4), 589-606.
about.ref3: Jamieson, G. A. & Vicente, K. J. (2001). Ecological interface design for petrochemical applications: supporting operator adaptation, continuous learning, and distributed, collaborative work. Computers & Chemical Engineering, 25(7-8), 1055-1074.
about.ref4: ANSI/ISA-101.01-2015. Human Machine Interfaces for Process Automation Systems. International Society of Automation.
about.ref5: Caño de las Heras, S. et al. (2021). A framework for the development of Pedagogical Process Simulators (P2Si) using explanatory models and gamification. Computers & Chemical Engineering, 151, 107350.
about.ref6: Cameron, I. T. et al. (2019). Education in Process Systems Engineering: Why it matters more than ever and how it can be structured. Computers & Chemical Engineering, 126, 102-112.
about.founderBody: Biochemical engineer building process visualization that works for students, operators, and safety engineers.
about.supportBody: If this project helps your lab, classroom, or plant training, you can chip in any amount. Donations go toward hosting, development, and making process visualization accessible.
